clue.text: Persian nightingale shot in the heart twice, would you say?

indicators.note: twice asks for the word to be given two times in a row
the question asks how the words would be spoken, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

parts.note: a shot in the heart of a target is a bull, short for bullseye

explanation.surface: A songbird from Persia is apparently shot through the heart, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: A shot in the centre of a target is a bull (bullseye); say 'bull bull' and you hear the bird's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bulbul is a songbird of Asia and Africa, celebrated in Persian poetry as a nightingale.

clue.text: A glass overhead showing King in sightly array

indicators.note: the king's letter goes inside the rearranged word
the letters of the word sightly are set out in a new array or order

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A pane above us displays a monarch in a pleasing arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'array' rearranges SIGHTLY to SYLIGHT, and 'in' puts K just after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof is a pane of glass above one's head.

clue.text: How the usurer handled the situation when stony

definitions.text: How the usurer handled the situation when stony

parts.words: How the usurer handled the situation when stony
parts.note: a moneylender pushes debtors hard for repayment, while stony (stony-broke) describes someone short of cash

explanation.surface: A moneylender's approach to a debtor with empty pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: Two senses meet: a usurer presses people for money, and someone stony-broke is short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard up means lacking cash, which is what stony-broke means; a usurer also squeezes debtors for payment.

clue.text: A general pardon set many free

indicators.note: the letters of set many are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A blanket pardon releases large numbers of prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges the seven letters of SET MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon granted to a whole class of offenders at once is a general amnesty.

clue.text: 10 suitable for Dartmouth or Sandhurst

parts.note: 10 points to the entry meaning cloth, and Dartmouth and Sandhurst are colleges training naval and army leaders

explanation.surface: Cloth fit for Britain's naval or army training colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is cloth, another word for which is material; Dartmouth (Royal Navy) and Sandhurst (Army) are Britain's colleges that train officers, so cadets with promise are this.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone judged to have the qualities to become a commissioned leader in the forces is described this way.

clue.text: A second-class highway overseas

parts.note: B denotes second class, after A
a highway is a road

explanation.surface: A minor B-road leads across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a foreign country, especially across the sea, is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Place given tenant below the rank of captain

indicators.note: the clue says this word, given the word tenant, makes the rank below captain, so tenant is taken away from that rank

parts.note: the army rank just below captain is a lieutenant
taken as written

explanation.surface: A position is handed to a junior officer who is not yet a captain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'place, given TENANT, makes the rank below captain': remove TENANT from LIEUTENANT and the place is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu of means in place of, so the French loanword means place.

clue.text: A dollar for a stag?

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for an American dollar and also names a male deer.

clue.text: Woolly branded butter

definitions.meaning: a marked male sheep, a woolly animal carrying its owner's brand
one who butts with the head

explanation.definitionFit: A male sheep is woolly and a notorious head-butter.

clue.text: A sort of 8 9 manufactured cloth

definitions.meaning: the two entries 8 and 9 joined name buckram, a stiff cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiffened textile, and the general word for woven textile covers it.

clue.text: Blouse ripped: any sign of the dagger?

indicators.note: a ripped garment is torn apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A torn top raises the question of whether a knife was used.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped' rearranges BLOUSE; the obelus (†) is the dagger mark used in printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger-shaped printer's mark, used for footnotes or to flag doubtful passages.

clue.text: The words that could bring play to a close

definitions.text: The words that could bring play to a close

parts.words: The words that could bring play to a close
parts.note: a speech spoken at the end of a drama, not the end of a game

explanation.surface: Words that might end a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing speech delivered to the audience after a drama ends.

clue.text: How track officials lowered standards and brought racing cars to a halt

definitions.text: How track officials lowered standards and brought racing cars to a halt

parts.words: How track officials lowered standards and brought racing cars to a halt
parts.note: standards are flags lowered by marshals, and waving flags signals cars to stop

explanation.surface: Race marshals relaxed their standards and stopped the cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowered standards' sounds like slackness, but standards are flags, and waving a flag at a car stops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Signalling vehicles to stop by waving flags at them is the sense meant.

clue.text: We hold naught for Cassandra's prophecy

indicators.note: the word we holds the zero inside it

parts.note: taken as written
naught (nought) is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: We keep nothing back as the prophetess speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassandra, the Trojan prophetess, foretold disaster that nobody believed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra foretold only grief and calamity, so her prophecy is misery.

clue.text: Exploded and departed

definitions.meaning: a bomb or gun that fired

explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that exploded and a person who left both did this.

clue.text: add energy to energy

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'add energy to energy (3)': E + GO gives the letters but no clue word defines them; the clue looks cut short at the start (probably 'I add energy...').

clue.text: Breathtaking order: "Zero therms!"

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: zero is the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astonishing instruction: no more gas units!
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges O plus THERMS. 'Breathtaking' is read as stopping someone's breath, a verbal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate someone is literally to take their breath away.

clue.text: Wooden platter found in ditch (I think!)

parts.note: a ditch is a trench
er is the hesitant sound of someone thinking

explanation.surface: A wooden plate turns up in a ditch, or so I believe.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher is an old wooden board or plate on which food was served.

clue.text: We hang around at all events

indicators.note: the word for hang goes around the other piece

parts.note: to hang in the air is to hover
taken as written

explanation.surface: We loiter about at every event.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean nevertheless or in any case.

clue.text: Bobby has an outsize sleeve -there's no getting away from it!

definitions.text: Bobby has an outsize sleeve -there's no getting away from it!

parts.words: Bobby has an outsize sleeve -there's no getting away from it!
parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, and the reach of the police is pictured as a very long limb

explanation.surface: A policeman with an oversized sleeve: escape is impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is British slang for a police officer; the phrase pictures police power as a long limb no criminal can escape.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the far-reaching power of the police to catch offenders.

clue.text: Top people's dwelling probably lit by a 2

definitions.text: Top people's dwelling probably lit by a 2

parts.words: Top people's dwelling probably lit by a 2
parts.note: people living at the top of a house occupy a room under the roof, lit by a window in it (2 refers to that entry)

explanation.surface: The elite's home is likely lit from above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top people' sounds like the elite, but they are just the ones living at the top of the house; 2 is the roof window.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic room at the top of a house, often lit by a window in the roof.

clue.text: A Kipling character talking to a goose when out at elbow

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel
someone too timid to say boo to a goose; bo is the word said

explanation.surface: A character from Kipling chats to a goose, elbows out.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'can't say bo (boo) to a goose' describes a very timid person.
explanation.definitionFit: With hands on hips and elbows turned outward is the posture described.

clue.text: Ease from position of terror .

indicators.note: the letters of ease from are put in a new position

explanation.surface: Relief from a terrifying situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'position' rearranges EASE FROM; 'of terror' is read as an adjective, causing dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening inspires dread.

clue.text: Part of a helmsman's timbers

indicators.note: only a part of the words is taken, the letters running inside them

explanation.surface: Some of a ship's steersman's wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' points to the letters inside hELMSman.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm trees give hardwood, so their name stands for timbers.

clue.text: … spring back, getting wind up again?

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to wind up is to coil

explanation.surface: Bouncing back, as if wound up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun or spring that jumps backwards on release does this.

clue.text: French physicist making bilingual announcement of fatherhood

parts.note: 'I am' in English gives am
pere is French for father, the second language

explanation.surface: A French scientist declares in two languages that he is a dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I am père': am is English, père French for father, together naming André-Marie Ampère.
explanation.definitionFit: André-Marie Ampère was the French scientist who studied electromagnetism; the unit of current is named after him.

clue.text: She shows Evita has lost it

indicators.note: the word Evita loses some letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The musical's heroine has lost her edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' takes IT out of EVITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a woman's name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Czech currency flowing into Germany

parts.note: currency here means a current, a river rising in Czechia and running through Germany

explanation.surface: Czech money pouring into Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' suggests money, but here it is something with a current: the river that rises in the Czech Republic and flows into Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: This great European river rises in the Czech mountains and crosses Germany to the North Sea.
